scenarios.name: standalone-isolation
scenarios.expected: the canonical manager creates, lists and completes a worktree in a repository without consumer state
scenarios.observed: create, list and complete succeed; the repository has no consumer directory and no legacy reference

scenarios.name: no-legacy-mirrors
scenarios.expected: no operation writes the legacy backup directory or the legacy backup references
scenarios.observed: after create, complete, cleanup and prune the legacy directory does not exist and the legacy references are empty

scenarios.name: legacy-preserve-dirty
scenarios.expected: the legacy preserveDirty value is applied and declared, the destination changes are preserved and no mirror is created
scenarios.observed: the compatibility notice is published on stderr, the destination changes are preserved, the worktree change is integrated and no mirror exists

scenarios.name: invalid-legacy-config-blocks
scenarios.observed: exit code 3, the worktree is preserved, the base is unchanged and no mirror exists

scenarios.name: explicit-config-wins
scenarios.expected: the explicit configuration is used, the legacy configuration is declared as ignored and the operation is not blocked
scenarios.observed: the operation succeeds, the notice names the ignored legacy configuration and the destination changes are preserved

scenarios.name: legacy-recover-import
scenarios.expected: the legacy transaction is imported once, the canonical manager recovers it and the legacy copy is not written back
scenarios.observed: the import is declared, the transaction is in the canonical state, the legacy journal is byte-identical and a second recovery does not import again

scenarios.name: conflict-blocks
scenarios.expected: exit code 5 without any mutation when the identity or the reference differs
scenarios.observed: exit code 5, the canonical and the legacy records are preserved and no transaction is created for a conflicting reference

scenarios.name: flowtask-env-inert
scenarios.expected: the legacy environment variables do not change the configuration, the authorization or the execution
scenarios.observed: the published output is identical with and without the legacy environment, the counter is not created and no mirror exists

standalone_isolation.mcp_handshake: initialize and tools/list publish seven tools
standalone_isolation.observed: the manager answers the version and the seven tools without the consumer, without Engram and without a consumer checkout

generic_locations.expected: the canonical state is used and no legacy artifact is written
generic_locations.observed: the state is published in the canonical state root and the legacy directory and references stay absent

legacy_preserve_dirty.expected: the legacy value is translated and declared
legacy_preserve_dirty.observed: preserve_dirty=true is applied from the translated configuration and the notice is published

invalid_legacy_config_blocks.observed: exit code 3 with both resources preserved

explicit_config_wins.expected: the explicit configuration is used and the legacy one is declared as ignored
explicit_config_wins.observed: the operation succeeds and the notice is published

legacy_recover_import.expected: one import into the canonical state and no copy back
legacy_recover_import.observed: one import, byte-identical legacy record, no second import

conflict_blocks.observed: exit code 5 with both resources preserved

flowtask_env_inert.observed: identical published output and no legacy artifact

repeated_update.expected: the installation and the update preserve the configuration, the worktrees, the journals, the backups and the references
repeated_update.observed: the installer suite reports 65 of 66 tests and the only failure is the known type error present before this increment

equivalence.expected: the command line and the stdio transport publish the same request and the same envelope for every cell
equivalence.observed: 48 cells published, all of them ok, and 58 tests with no failure

limits.statement: The build tip of the standalone manager is present in the local build clone and in the materialised submodule, but it is not published in the standalone origin, so a reconstruction from the remote alone is not possible.

The manifest of the previous phase is absent and its digest is only known by its prefix, so no verdict is published for it; the committed evidence of the previous phase and its six verified digests substitute it.
The base of the delivery is the frozen commit of the previous phase; a delivery over the moved main requires a rebase and a complete revalidation.
